reason: The hypothesis directly restates the finding from P1, P4, P6, and P30 that fine-grained CoCrFeMnNi HEA exhibits better wear resistance than coarse-grained due to a more stable oxide layer, merely proposing a pre-treatment to achieve that grain size rather than studying it as-received. The mechanism, predicted outcome, and overall idea are taken almost verbatim from these passages, with the addition of a controlled pre-treatment and a falsification test that are obvious next steps. The mention of inverse Hall-Petch from P3 is used only as a boundary condition, not as a novel integration.
copied_elements: fine grain size HEA has better wear resistance than coarse grain due to high surface strength (P1, P4)
oxide layer on coarse grain cracks under load, increasing friction and wear (P1, P4, P6, P30)
fine grain sample forms more rupture-resistant oxide layer (P6, P30)
oxide film acts as lubricating layer reducing friction (P33)
inverse Hall-Petch softening in ultra-nanocrystalline regime (P3)
